newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine maize export sales 6 mln T - trade.
newsitem.headline: Argentine maize export sales 6 mln T - trade.

text.p: Argentine exporters have sold about six million tonnes of 1996/97 maize to foreign buyers so far this season, traders said Thursday.
"Up to last Friday, we calculated a total of about six million tonnes already sold for export, with around 3.5 million tonnes already shipped," one trader told Reuters.
He said the biggest buyers were Iran, with 650,000 tonnes, Indonesia, with 550,000 tonnes, South Korea and Egypt, each with 500,000 tonnes, and Venezuela, with 400,000 tonnes.
Other traders said that export sales totaled 6.2 to 6.3 million tonnes. One said he thought sales to Iran could be as much as 1.3 million tonnes, but another dismissed this idea.
"We heard this week they had bought South African maize, so I think that 1.3 million tonnes of Argentine to Iran is completely out of the question," he said.
His figure for Iranian purchases was 650,000 tonnes, and he said the other biggest buyers of Argentine maize were Indonesia, Egypt, South Korea and Malaysia.

Most traders were optimistic about the shape of the maize crop, which is now mainly harvested, saying that good yields in southern Buenos Aires had partially made up for losses further north due to Rio Cuarto virus.
"We have a production estimate of 14.5 million tonnes, but if you asked me if I had to raise it or cut it, I'd raise it. We are optimistic about the maize," he said.

Another trader was even more bullish, predicting output of 15.2 million tonnes. He added he thought the government's Agricultural Secretariat would raise its estimate of output, currently at 14.4 million tonnes, when it announces its new crop forecasts in the next few days.
"They'll boost their forecast because it was based on normal yields around Necochea, and the yields have been better than normal," he said.
But, while export sales are well advanced and the crop is coming along nicely, traders said Argentine maize is too expensive to be competitive for the moment on world markets.
"At these prices, things are difficult," one said, "We haven't seen much done for about 10 days."

He said FOB Argentine maize was going for $15 over Chicago Board of Trade July basis for May to June shipment. He said the difference with U.S. corn at $23 over was insufficient to make up for lower freight prices from the United States to major markets.
The Agriculture Secretariat predicts total maize exports this season of 9.5 million tonnes. It said earlier Thursday that 77.1 percent of the maize had been harvested by May 9.
